subject: MAP: Re-sequencing evaluation slate and acceptance window (Sierra)
messages:
From: Amelia Park <amelia.park@sierrahealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: manuel.ortega@sierrahealth.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 19 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP timeline: procurement hold impacting acceptance window

Hi Karthik,

Quick note from procurement — our internal security review pushed the hosting approval back by two weeks. That shifts our planned acceptance window and the evaluation dates in the MAP. Manual told me to flag any downstream impacts from Redwood's side (SLA/credits, short-term validation support).

Can you confirm whether the evaluation gating (live inference tests + integration verification) can compress to a single week if we keep the same scope? Also, if there are deployment priorities you need to surface to help us keep the original close target, please share.

Attachments: Sierra_MAP_v1.pdf (pdf, MAP v1)

Thanks,
Amelia Park
Director, Procurement
Sierra Health Systems
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: Amelia Park <amelia.park@sierrahealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 19 Jun 2025 10:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP timeline: procurement hold impacting acceptance window

Amelia — thanks for the heads up and for sending the MAP.

Short answer: we can compress some eval steps but there are tradeoffs we should call out. Proposed quick options: 
- Option A (conservative): shift acceptance window by two weeks, keep full live inference tests (recommended for safety/regression checks).
- Option B (compressed): run targeted integration + smoke tests in 5 working days, Redwood provides an on-call validation engineer during the week of testing and a follow-up soft-acceptance for 48 hours. This reduces certificate of performance scope (no extended load runs).

I’ll loop in internal ops to confirm capacity and whether we can prioritize Sierra infra for that test week. If you need an exec note for procurement to escalate, I can prepare and copy Marissa.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

> Attachment: Reviewed_Sierra_MAP_notes.txt (text)
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 19 Jun 2025 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: Sierra — procurement pushed hosting approval by ~2w (MAP re-sequence ask)

Team — FYI, procurement at Sierra moved their hosting sign-off out two weeks, which materially impacts our planned eval/acceptance window. Key asks below: 
1) Can we reserve a validation engineer and a dedicated test pool for week of Jul 7 (preferred compressed window)?
2) If we support the compressed Option B, what failure-modes do we need to call out in the MAP (e.g., no full-load run; reduced KV-cache warmup)?
3) Is there room to offer a small close-credit or extended support window if they accept a compressed validation? Marissa, happy to draft the exec escalation.

Initial risk log for this thread (high-level):
- Risk A: Acceptance slip increases post-go-live defects (medium-high)
- Risk B: Procurement timeline uncertainty triggers broader schedule drift (medium)
- Risk C: Lack of dedicated infra in test week reduces confidence scores (medium-high)

Please reply with availability — I want to lock an internal decision before I reply back to Amelia with a single suggested path.

Karthik
From: Manuel Ortega <manuel.ortega@sierrahealth.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: amelia.park@sierrahealth.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 20 Jun 2025 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP timeline: procurement hold impacting acceptance window

Karthik — appreciate the fast response. Procurement is amenable to Option B (compressed) if Redwood can guarantee an on-call engineer and a short remediation window after soft acceptance. They also requested that Redwood highlight any specific acceptance criteria we waive or reduce in writing.

We can shift the MAP acceptance window to start Jul 7 and be flexible on exact close date if the validation proves successful. Attached is a lightly-updated MAP showing the requested re-sequence (Updated_EvalPlan_v2.xlsx).

Cheers,
Manuel
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 21 Jun 2025 15:04:00 -0700
Subject: Internal escalation draft for exec (Sierra MAP re-sequence)

Karthik/Laura — I reviewed the risks. Draft note for exec escalation below; I recommend we send this from Pete or Sarah with a cc to Amelia to ensure procurement sees the ask as material. 

Draft exec escalation (short):
- Ask: Exec support to prioritize validation capacity for Sierra Health (week of Jul 7) and approval to offer a $12,500 one-time close credit if Sierra agrees to compressed validation and soft-acceptance terms.
- Why: Procurement delay compresses the evaluation window. Without dedicated capacity and on-call engineering we expose the customer to higher post-acceptance defects and risk relationship goodwill.
- Mitigation: Redwood will provide: 1) a dedicated validation engineer for the test week; 2) a 48-hour soft-acceptance remediation window; 3) post-acceptance monitoring for 14 days at no charge.
- Metrics: target smoke-test pass rate >= 95% and zero P0 regressions during soft-accept window.

If you agree, I’ll hand this to Pete for signature. Also — Ben, confirm capacity for the validation pool (private cluster scheduling).

Marissa
[Inline attachments referenced above: Sierra_MAP_v1.pdf (pdf stub), Reviewed_Sierra_MAP_notes.txt (text stub), Updated_EvalPlan_v2.xlsx (xlsx stub)]
